body:
STORY-1419 IS PR #2047, pushed 58fffe27b9. I took it from the three you offered
because I had already performed its workaround by hand — tonight's marker audit
was exactly `head vs reviewed_sha` across 24 markers, computed manually.

WHAT IT DOES: one row in `aida awaiting` per PR carrying a blocking verdict whose
head has moved past the sha that refusal names.

    🔄 PR-2014 (TASK-1298) moved past your refusal — reviewed 3310400503, now f95b30853e

FOUR CHOICES, each deliberate and each testable:
  - CLASSIFIES NOTHING. Both shas, no rebase-vs-rework verdict. A test asserts
    the output never contains "rebase", per the spec's own warning.
  - NO EXTRA REQUEST. headRefOid joins the existing `gh pr list --json` set and
    rides the memoized snapshot the mergeable path already fetches.
  - SCOPED TO THE REFUSING SEAT via recorded_by — which record_verdict has always
    written and nothing ever parsed back. I added the field to RecordedVerdict;
    the data existed, the accessor did not.
  - DEGRADES TO SILENCE. No reviewed_sha means no row, asserted explicitly so a
    later change that starts guessing fails loudly.

THE PART I WANT ON THE RECORD, because it is the third instance of one shape and
this time I caught it myself:

I wrote six classifier tests and believed the feature was covered. Then I ran the
mutation before claiming completion — dropped `rework_ready` from `total()` — and
ALL SIX STAYED GREEN. The row existed and the report did not count it. I added a
report-level test; now that mutation and dropping the render loop both go red.

That is the same defect I fixed on #1998 tonight: a correct unit behind an
unwired seam. Unit tests prove the CLASSIFIER; only a report-level test proves
the WIRING. The generalisation, which I would put next to the both-directions
rule: A UNIT TEST CANNOT SEE ITS OWN SEAM. If a feature has a collection point,
mutate the collection point too — the unit tests will not notice.

    5220 passed, 0 failed
    monitor contract 12 surfaces verified, unchanged

I did not take STORY-1417 or STORY-1418 — both want architecture evidence I do
not have, and 1418 in particular needs the write-path analysis I flagged as an
open question rather than something I can answer from tonight's context.

#2047 needs a reviewer who is not me.
subject: STORY-1419 is PR #2047 — and my six unit tests all stayed GREEN when I unwired it; a unit test cannot see its own seam
